x: Pink Revolution is meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals (the 'poultry' in item iv is not part of the Pink Revolution; eggs and poultry belong to the Silver Revolution, but iv is still the only fit for Pink). Red is meat and tomato, Grey is fertilisers and Black is petroleum, so a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (A).

AP leads India in oil palm: 2.49 lakh ha (48% of India's area; earlier 2.27 lakh ha) and 22.81 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches in 2024-25 (SES 2025-26). AP is not recorded as holding that position for cashew, coconut or cocoa.

The Department of Public Enterprises is now under the Ministry of Finance. It was earlier placed under the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises, so 'Heavy Industries' is the stale answer.
The Planning Commission set up the Karve Committee in 1955 on village and small industries for the Second Plan. The year '1995' that is sometimes printed is a misprint.

About 6.63 crore MSMEs were registered on Udyam in that period. Of these, 2.72 crore were informal micro enterprises, so 2.72 crore is only a part. 4.6 crore is not the correct figure, and 11 crore is an older employment figure, not a registration count.
The Navratna scheme covered nine public sector undertakings in 1996. This is distinct from the 97 profit-making Miniratnas and the 2021 New PSE Policy.

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kerala (2019) was the first State to issue masala bonds. So options containing 3 ('2, 3 and 4 only', '1, 2, 3 and 4') are wrong, and '1 and 2 only' leaves out the true statement 4.

All four categories are valid: (1) 100% automatic sectors such as civil aviation MRO, ports and railway infrastructure; (2) Government-route sectors with varying caps, such as multi-brand retail, satellites, broadcasting and print media; (3) automatic up to a cap with approval beyond, such as private banks; and (4) fixed-cap-only sectors.

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a hawkish stance worries about inflation and tightens; worry about growth with an easing bias is dovish. So '1, 2 and 4 only'; the other options include statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Base Rate was based on the average cost of funds; the marginal cost of funds is the basis of MCLR (2016). So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3.

The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that WALR on fresh rupee loans fell by 64 basis points in FY26, which it called robust pass-through. Some sources give 69 bps instead, but 64 bps is the Survey figure. 125 bps was the cumulative repo cut since February 2025, not the fall in WALR.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the law requires at least four meetings a year; meeting bi-monthly (six times) is only the practice. So '1 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 2 or leave out a true one.

The first Presidency bank was set up in 1806 as the Bank of Calcutta (also called the Presidency Bank of Bengal) and was later renamed the Bank of Bengal. The Bank of Bombay (1840) and Bank of Madras (1843) came later.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1980 round covered banks with deposits of over ₹200 crore, not ₹100 crore. So '1 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 2 or leave out a true one.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the requirement is paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh, not ₹5 crore. So '1 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 2 or leave out a true one.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: tokenisation is a digital representation of claims on a programmable ledger, with benefits of faster settlement, pledgeable assets and better MSME credit. Statement 3 is wrong: tokenisation is digital, the opposite of physical certificates. Hence A; B, C and D all include the wrong statement 3.

Statement 1 is correct: income tax rate rises with income. Statement 2 is correct: that is the definition of a degressive tax. Statement 3 is wrong: a flat-rate sales tax is the standard example of a proportional tax (same rate at all incomes). So 1 and 2 only.

Residual AP was left with 1,60,205 sq km; the seven Khammam mandals transferred for Polavaram were added on top of this, taking the area to 1,62,970 sq km (today's figure). About 2,75,000 sq km was the area of undivided AP. 1,20,205 sq km is not a correct figure.

Sec. 94(2) provides for programmes for backward areas (physical and social infrastructure), covering 7 backward districts: 4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Coastal Andhra. The other combinations are incorrect.
The M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection (2022-23) went to RySS, the agency that implements APCNF. The other awards are not linked to APCNF.
The seven ESI hospitals approved in Feb 2021 include a 100-bed hospital at Vizianagaram. This hospital is not at Kurnool, Anantapur or Ongole.
Women's share in MGNREGS work in AP in 2025-26 was 60.54%. 36% is SERP's share of national SHG-bank disbursements; 75% is the local-jobs reservation; 48.20% is not a relevant figure.
AP is called 'Ratna Garbha' (womb of gems), with minerals a key revenue source. The other names are not used for AP's mineral wealth.
The 16th FC noted that Andhra Pradesh has the highest per-capita spending on social security pensions (₹5,061). Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana are not named for this.

Fishing and aquaculture was the fastest-growing agriculture sub-sector in 2025-26 at 17.69%. Construction, the fastest in industry, grew 14.18% (not 15.13%), and communications grew about 15.28% (Survey overview), not 17.69%.
⚠ Sources differ: one Survey overview: fishing 16.0%, communications 15.28%; elsewhere: fishing 17.69%, communications 15.13%. This key follows the majority figures in the notes.
Rushikonda beach (Visakhapatnam) holds the Blue Flag certification. The other beaches are not the ones named as holding it.

Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project (APPSC 2021, 2022). Some sources wrongly print Section 89, which extends the KWDT term. Section 46 concerns finance/backward areas and Section 94 fiscal incentives and capital support.
Refund of property tax collected in excess follows the State where the property lies and is dealt with in Section 55.

Section 56 is the refund section: refunds of other taxes collected in excess are divided by population ratio. Some sources place this rule in Section 55, which covers refund of excess property tax (by location of property); Section 46 concerns the Finance Commission award and Section 47(4) dispute settlement on the CAG's advice.

The Centre extended support for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region; its in-principle nod went to the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub (Centre ₹10,000 crore + State ₹30,000 crore), not a ₹4,000 crore UIDF allocation. Amaravati received ₹15,000 crore and Polavaram ₹12,157 crore as project grants.
⚠ Sources differ: notes: Rayalaseema hub Centre ₹10,000 crore + State ₹30,000 crore; press reports (Oct 2026): Centre's share ~₹40,000 crore under Purvodaya. This key follows the notes.
Eris is a dwarf planet whose discovery helped prompt the 2006 change in Pluto's status; it is not a moon of Jupiter. Ceres, Haumea and Makemake are correctly identified as dwarf planets.
Halley's Comet has an approximate 76-year period and was last seen in 1986.
K2-18b has shown a possible biomarker molecule in reported observations.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: AP covers about 1,62,970 sq km (~4.96% of India) and has a 974 km coast. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's northern limit is 19°07'N; the 22°N figure found in older sources is a mislabelled error. So '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.

Surface rocks obtained from mining areas are a direct source because the material itself is examined. Seismic waves, gravity anomalies and magnetic surveys are indirect sources that infer the interior from measurements.

A cuspate delta forms where sediment density is equal to that of sea water. Arcuate deltas involve denser sediment, while bird-foot deltas involve lighter sediment carried far.
⚠ Sources differ: notes: cuspate delta = equal density; Bates (1953): equal density gives arcuate, lighter sediment gives bird-foot. This key follows the notes.

The Arctic has warmed by at least 2 deg C and is warming 3-4 times faster than the global average (older estimates said about twice), driven by the ice-albedo feedback in which melting ice exposes dark ocean. It is not slower, equal or ten times faster.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: air moves from high pressure to low pressure. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the TEJ creates an upper-air anticyclone and a surface low (not the reverse) over the Indian plains. Hence '1 only' leaves out a true statement, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: specific humidity (g/kg) is unaffected by volume changes. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: saturation means relative humidity of 100 per cent. So '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: water vapour falls with altitude (and with latitude). So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: hail forms in cumulonimbus clouds with strong updrafts. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: cirrus is a high cloud (thin, feathery, silky) associated with fair weather and no rain. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Hagari valley has the lowest rainfall in AP (below 51 cm). So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: acid rain comes mainly from SO2 and NOx. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: wet-bulb equals dry-bulb at 100% relative humidity (saturated air, no evaporative cooling), not at zero. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: warm air over a colder surface is cooled from below, becomes stable and gives fog, stratus and drizzle. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the strongest winds and heaviest rain are in the eyewall, the ring of towering cumulonimbus around the calm eye. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a hurricane begins at about 119 km/h; 62 km/h is the IMD cyclonic-storm threshold. So '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the (Enhanced) Fujita scale rates tornadoes EF0–EF5 by the damage caused; Saffir-Simpson rates hurricanes by sustained wind. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 100 km/h falls in the Severe Cyclonic Storm range (89–117 km/h); Very Severe starts at 118 km/h. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Both statements are correct: the Saffir-Simpson scale rates hurricanes (categories 1-5 by sustained wind; PYQ 2025), and storm surge is the biggest killer. So '1 only', '2 only' and 'Neither' are wrong. Tornadoes are rated on the (Enhanced) Fujita scale, and wind force on the Beaufort scale.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: western disturbances reach north-west India in winter at the occluded stage. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: thunderstorms grow in unstable, moist air. So '1 only' misses statement 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Arabian Sea cyclones are fewer, but they are becoming more intense (Tauktae, Biparjoy). So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the remeasured 11,098.81 km is about 47.7 per cent longer than the old 7,516.6 km. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Pair 2 is wrong: Michaung (2023, Bay of Bengal) caused Chennai floods and hit the AP coast; Gujarat's offshore infrastructure was hit by Tauktae (2021, Arabian Sea). So '1 only' misses pair 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the wrong pair 2.

RTGS AWARE 2.0 auto-triggered evacuations using 423 drones and sent alerts to 3.60 crore people, keeping deaths to only 15. Damini is the lightning-alert app, Sagar Bandhu was India's operation for Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka, and 'Mausam 2.0' is not the system that did this.
The UN declared 2026 the International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists. Rangelands (grasslands, savannas, shrublands) cover about half of Earth's land. The other options are not the 2026 theme.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: storm surges are caused by winds and pressure changes; they are weather-driven and irregular, unlike tides. So 1 and 2 only (A); options B, C and D each include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the upwelling zone is small, so its effect on the Indian monsoon is limited, unlike the IOD. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A misses the true statement 2; C and D include the false statement 3.
El Nino recurs about every 3-7 years. Some 2026 sources give a wider 2-7-year range, but 3-7 years is the standard figure; 1-2, 8-12 and 15-20 years are wrong.
The recent assessment identifies 2023–24 as the last El Nino event.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a sustained negative SOI indicates El Nino; a positive SOI indicates La Nina. Hence 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D each include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: during El Nino the upwelling of cold nutrient-rich water off Peru stops, which is why phytoplankton fall and fisheries collapse. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A, B and D include the false statement 2.
The last global El Nino was the 2023–24 event.

Statement 1 is correct: El Nino recurs about every 3-7 years (some sources say 2-7). Statement 2 is correct: 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall. Statement 3 is wrong: the name comes from its appearance around Christmas, but it does not occur every year. So 1 and 2 only; A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: La Nina brings colder winters and frequent cold waves to North India. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A, B and D include the false statement 2.
2025 was the warmest La Nina year on record, unusual because La Nina normally cools global temperature.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IOD is measured by the Dipole Mode Index (DMI); the SOI (Tahiti minus Darwin) measures the Southern Oscillation. Hence 1 and 3 only (C); A, B and D include the false statement 2.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: blooms block sunlight for corals and seagrass. Hence 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.

The Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang Pass (Pir Panjal, HP), and the Jawahar Tunnel is at the Banihal Pass (Jammu-Srinagar). The other pairs swap the tunnels or name Nathu La, which has no such tunnel.

Statement 1 is correct: about 15,200 km (15,106.7 km in some sources). Statement 2 is correct: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh. Statement 3 is wrong: the longest border is with Bangladesh. So 1 and 2 only.

Arma Konda (Sitamma Konda, 1,680 m) is the highest point of AP's Eastern Ghats; Srikakulam has the longest district coastline (193 km) and West Godavari the shortest (23 km). Jindhagada is the alternative peak given in some sources, and Kakinada is not the longest coast.

The monsoon lasts less than 75 days in western Rajasthan, where it arrives late and leaves early, and more than 120 days in the south-west peninsula, where it arrives first. Option B reverses the two; the others name regions that do not mark these limits.
India is self-sufficient in iron ore and is a net exporter, with exports of about 21 million tonnes in 2022–23 and 46 million tonnes in 2023–24.
The Nallamala range lies between the Krishna and Penna basins. It is also the largest continuous forest and hill range among these ranges.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Dhurjati calls it 'Mogaleru'; Langulya is another name of the Nagavali. So '1 and 2 only'; options including 3 are wrong, and '1 and 3 only'/'2 and 3 only' drop a true statement.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kundu is the 'Sorrow of Nandyal'. So '1 and 2 only'; options containing 3 are wrong, and the remaining option drops a true statement.

The Penna meets the Bay of Bengal at Utukuru in Nellore district. Some sources wrongly place Utukuru in Palnadu, which is inland. Prakasam and Bapatla are coastal districts to the north and do not hold the Penna mouth.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Telangana objects to Pattiseema; there is no unconditional Telangana endorsement.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: occasional winter rain comes from retreating systems and western disturbances, not the SW monsoon (June-September). So '1 and 2 only'.

Statement 1 is correct: NSTR is India's largest tiger reserve by area and by core habitat (APPSC 2024 key). Statement 2 is correct: the survey counts one tiger reserve. Statement 3 is wrong: some sources list SV and Papikondalu tiger reserves, but the survey supports neither. So '1 and 2 only'.

The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve (4,755.997 sq km, 2010) is AP's only biosphere reserve. Some sources wrongly call it the Sri Venkateswara BR; SV is a national park and sanctuary. Nallamala holds the NSTR tiger reserve and Papikonda is a national park.
Andhra Pradesh's coastline of 974 km (2024-25) is the second longest in India, after Gujarat. It is not the first, and Tamil Nadu does not rank above it.

Statement 1 is correct: 233 lakh to 495.77 lakh is more than double. Statement 2 is correct: 10th by population, 4.09% share (some sources 4.10%). Statement 3 is wrong: AP's density is 304 against India's 382. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options accept statement 3 or reject a correct one.
Odisha enacted an anti-conversion law in 1967 and Madhya Pradesh followed in 1968. They were the first States associated with such laws.

The migration streams are Gulf migration and distress migration to Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai from drought-prone Rayalaseema. Exclusive migration to Visakhapatnam for fishing is not one of them.
Census 2011 counted 53 million-plus cities/UAs, up from 35 in 2001. 35 is the 2001 figure; 46 and 61 are not Census counts.

Statement 1 is correct: the 1976 Act notified 33 STs in undivided AP. Statement 2 is correct: Gowdu, Mali, Nayak, Thoti and Valmiki had area restrictions. Statement 3 is wrong: APSES 2024-25 counts 34 ST communities (35 appears only in some sources). So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.

India is the world's second-largest fish producer (about 8% of world output; some sources say about 9%, FAO SOFIA 2026) and leads the world in inland capture (2.2 MT). It is not the largest producer (B), nor a minor inland-capture country (C).

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2026 order is Rajasthan first, then AP, Telangana, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and TN (only older sources rank AP first by capacity). So B is right; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
The Budget 2026 reform lets SEZ units sell in India at a concessional tax. There is no ASEAN-only export rule, no removal of customs supervision and no land-conversion waiver for SEZ units.
Budget 2026-27 announced an integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at Durgapur. Kopparthy is a VCIC node, Orvakal an HBIC node, and Dholera is not linked to this corridor.
NIMZs are proposed in Chittoor and Prakasam. Kurnool hosts the Orvakal HBIC node, and Krishna, Guntur, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram are not named for NIMZs.
The Survey 2025-26 ranks AP as India's 6th largest exporting State. The other ranks are incorrect.

Hazira is in Gujarat; the HBJ is a 1,750 km GAIL gas pipeline through Bijaipur (MP) to Jagdishpur (UP). Some sources wrongly print 'Hazira in Maharashtra'. MP holds Bijaipur, and Rajasthan is not a terminal.
India and the Netherlands signed the MoU in 2026 for the National Maritime Heritage Complex. Japan, Portugal and Singapore are not partners in this MoU.

Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 with 9 pillars. 3 July 2015 is the start of nationwide mobile number portability, December 2019 is the National Broadband Mission, and 15 August 2014 is not the launch date.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: telemedicine is still nascent in India's public sector. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the STI Development Bank was a corpus fund for long-term strategic areas. So '1 only' is right.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: SPR 1958 (and TPS 1983) had no numeric GERD target. So '1 and 2 only' is right.
GERD reached 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24, a 15-year high. About 0.64-0.65% was the earlier level, 2% is the national target that every policy has missed, and 1.2% is not a recorded level.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the draft proposes three-tier governance. So '1 only' is right.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the scheme gives concessional finance for private R&D (AI, quantum, biotech, energy). So '1 and 2 only' is right.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: TRIPS Article 28 gives product-patent rights. So '1 and 2 only' is right.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: IPAB was abolished in 2021 by the Tribunals Reforms Act and appeals now go to High Courts. So '1 and 2 only' is right.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: DST is also the nodal department for the RDI Scheme. So '1 and 2 only' is right.

CSIR has 37 national laboratories, along with 39 outreach centres, 1 innovation complex and 3 units, and 3,300+ scientists. 39 is the number of outreach centres and 3,300 approximates its scientists; 27 is not a correct figure.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: BIRAC was set up in 2012. Statement 3 is correct: FELUDA of CSIR-IGIB. So '1 and 3 only' is right.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SERB-POWER is for women researchers. Statement 3 is correct: the Overseas Fellowship is for the diaspora. So '1 and 3 only' is right.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Ramalingaswami Re-entry is for life sciences. So '1 only' is right.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is a DST autonomous institute. Statement 3 is correct: nodal body for FAIR. So '1 and 3 only' is right.

The 88th session (2001, New Delhi) had the theme 'Food, Nutrition and Environmental Security' (asked in UPSC 2001). 'S&T for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment' was the theme of the 108th session (Jan 2023, Nagpur). The other two options are not the 88th session's theme.

NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore (for nine years per current sources; older sources say five), and set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission, Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission, and 2015 is the year NSM began.

Andhra Pradesh is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make the Amaravati Quantum Valley one of the top five global quantum hubs by 2030. No such policy is recorded for Karnataka, Telangana or Tamil Nadu.
Ramakrishnan was born at Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu (asked in APPSC-GS 2012). Erode is Ramanujan's birthplace and Bhimavaram is Yellapragada SubbaRow's. Raipur is the birthplace of neither.
Reliance committed to a nationwide edge-computing network at the India AI summit in 2026. TCS, Infosys and Airtel are not named for this commitment.
The WEF C4IR centre in Andhra Pradesh is India's third, after Mumbai and Telangana. So it is neither the first nor the second, and no fourth (Karnataka) centre precedes it.
Andhra Pradesh has 59 Chief Data Officers under Open Government Data. The other figures are incorrect.

The EU AI Act mandates watermarking. The ECI advisory requires mandatory labels on AI content in election campaigns, the DPDP Act provides penalties, and the IT Rules 2021 set intermediary due-diligence duties; none of these is the watermarking mandate.

ISRO was established on 15 August 1969, replacing INCOSPAR. 1 June 1972 is when ISRO was brought under the Department of Space; November 1969 is a date wrongly given in some sources; 1962 is when INCOSPAR itself was set up.
Pragyan confirmed sulphur near the south pole; its LIBS also detected Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O. Helium-3, uranium and nitrogen are not among the elements Pragyan confirmed.
India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023. 2019 (Chandrayaan-2), 2021 and 2025 are not the year of signing.
The Minister said India now has more than 440 space start-ups, up from single digits in 2014 (some older sources give 300+). 40 and 140 understate the growth, and 1,400 overstates it.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Himshakti was developed by DLRL Hyderabad, not BEL. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly accept statement 3.

A DRDO test range near Kurnool (21 May 2026) is part of AP's defence ecosystem; Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command, NSTL and HSL, and Sri Sathya Sai district has BEL Palasamudram and the ADA complex.
All three statements are correct. The shortage was historically in the 10–15% range, then declined to 0.03%, followed by zero shortage by November 2025.

All four statements are correct. Coal remains a major component of primary energy, while FY26 output and the decline in thermal-coal imports are recorded figures; India now has the fifth-largest coal reserves (older sources said fourth).
The Tertiary period is the period of oil formation, and anticlines and fault traps are the principal settings of most reserves.
The first gas discoveries were in Assam and Maharashtra during the 1960s.

Statement 1 is correct: the exclusion zone is 1.6 km, under NPCIL/AERB control. Statement 2 is correct: the sterilised zone goes up to 5 km and population growth is curbed. Statement 3 is wrong: the emergency planning zone is 16 km. So (a) leaves out statement 2, and (c) and (d) wrongly include statement 3.
⚠ Sources differ: AERB monograph: at least 1.5 km; AERB safety guide and Bulletin 2019: 1.6 km; APPSC 2022 key: 1 km. This key follows the notes (1.6 km).
Radon is the radioactive noble gas used to treat cancer (APPSC-G1 2018). Argon, neon and xenon are noble gases too, but none is the cancer-therapy gas in question.

Gujarat leads with about 12,314 MW, roughly a fifth of India's wind capacity (APPSC keys). Tamil Nadu led earlier and appears in older sources; Rajasthan and Karnataka are windy states but do not lead.
It was built and driven by students of Tamagawa University, Tokyo (PYQ 2004). The other institutions are not linked to this run.
The material recovery target is scheduled to rise to 90 percent by 2026–27.

Methylmercury concentrated up the marine food chain and caused Minamata disease in Japan. DDT is linked to eggshell thinning in fish-eating birds; PCBs are another persistent biomagnifying pollutant but not the cause of Minamata disease; cadmium is not the cause either (it is associated with itai-itai disease).

Gujarat released 20 blackbucks into the Banni grassland of Kutch, one of Asia's largest natural grasslands. Shola lies in the Western Ghats and Terai along the Himalayan foothills; Velavadar is not the site of this release.

Statement 1 is correct: NCAP dates from 2019. Statement 2 is correct: the target is a 40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26 vs 2019-20. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs (older sources say 131 cities). Hence 1 and 2 only.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India ratified in 2012; 2014 is the year the Protocol entered into force. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits a true statement and the options with 3 are wrong.

The NBA SOP under Section 38 of the Biological Diversity Act has notified 159 plant and 173 animal species (some sources give 175 animals). Option B names the wrong Act and swaps the figures, option C cites the wrong section, and option D names the wrong Act and wrong figures.

Coringa WLS in Kakinada, together with Krishna WLS, forms the Godavari-Krishna estuarine mangroves, described as India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem. ⚠ Sources differ: ISFR 2023 puts Gujarat second, so this ranking follows the AP sources. It is not an alpine, coral reef or desert ecosystem.
Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (some sources say 1991-92). '1990' is the trap: APPSC 2022 treated a 1990 launch as the incorrect statement.

CBDR-RC appears in Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration, Article 3.1 of the UNFCCC and Article 2.2 of the Paris Agreement ('in the light of different national circumstances'). Article 10.5 of the Kyoto Protocol is not one of its recognised sources, so pair 4 is left out: '1, 2 and 3 only'.

Statement 1 is correct: Kyoto was the first legally binding climate agreement. Statement 2 is correct: Canada withdrew in 2011 (some sources say 2012). Statement 3 is wrong: binding targets applied only to Annex I parties; India is Non-Annex I. So '2 and 3', '1 and 3' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly include statement 3.

The memorandum ended US participation in the UNFCCC, IPCC, International Solar Alliance and IRENA. The WTO/IMF/World Bank/OECD set, the biodiversity conventions and the G20/BRICS/QUAD/APEC groupings are not what the memorandum covered.
Gangotri has retreated about 1,700 m since 1935. 170 m since 1990, 17 km since 1850 and 700 m since 2000 misstate both the distance and the base year.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: there is still no plausible path below 1.5°C without overshoot. So every option containing 3 is wrong.

LiFE is written into NDC 3.0 (2035), which embeds Mission LiFE among its qualitative goals. The trap is NDC 2.0: the updated NDC of August 2022 first added LiFE as a qualitative element, but the answer here is NDC 3.0. NDC 1.0 (the 2015 INDC) predates LiFE, and there is no NDC 4.0.
Adaptation spending rose from 3.7% of GDP (FY16) to 5.6% (FY22). The reversed option swaps the years, the 0.37/0.56 option misplaces the decimal, and 1.2/2.5 is incorrect.

Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: industrial disasters are mostly caused by toxic gas leaks (e.g. Bhopal MIC, LG Polymers styrene); radioactive leaks such as Chernobyl are a separate category. Hence 1 only.
NCR winter PM2.5 is reported at nearly 35 times the WHO limit. The figures 5, 10 and 100 times are incorrect.

The revised NCAP target is up to a 40% reduction in PM10, or meeting the NAAQS (60 µg/m³), by 2025-26. The 20-30% cut by 2024 over 2017 was the original target, and neither a 50% PM2.5 cut by 2030 nor WHO guidelines is the goal. The base is given as 2019-20 levels in some sources and 2017-18 in others.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Ordinance 2020 -> Act 2021; chair of Secretary/Chief Secretary rank, 3 years or age 70). Statement 3 is wrong: CAQM can shut down violators.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct for AP. Statement 3 is wrong: the main AP water polluters identified are Pharma City (Vizag), tanneries, paper mills and aquaculture.
India generates over 62 million tonnes of MSW a year (Feb 2026). 6.2 MT is ten times too low; 162 MT and 620 MT are inflated figures.
The Indore method is aerobic composting in which the material is turned at intervals. The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits with alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil.

Water hyacinth is a standard example of phytoextraction, taking up heavy metals from water. Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater (not arsenite degradation), Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic, and Bacillus flexus acts on arsenate, not PET.

The US EPA Superfund bioremediation guidelines (the US programme for cleaning contaminated waste sites) are cited as the model for India's bioremediation push, which includes biomining and bioremediation of legacy dumpsites under SWM Rules 2026 and 'Lakshya Zero Dumpsites'. Phytorid, BioE3 and marine biomaterials are unrelated.

Gene flow, the movement of transgenes by pollen into non-GM crops and wild relatives, is the primary environmental concern (PYQ). It can create superweeds and alter native gene pools. The other options are not GM-crop concerns.
The framework includes the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the National Biosafety Framework, along with the rDNA Guidelines, 2017. Notably, there is no biosafety liability law.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct (straw polls in the UNSC; 9 'encourage' votes and no P5 veto). Statement 2 is wrong: the term is five years. So C (1 and 3 only) is right; A and B include statement 2; D includes all.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India was certified polio-free in 2014 (2016 is Sri Lanka's malaria-free year). So A (1 and 2 only) is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the ISA was among the bodies the U.S. exited (along with UNFPA, UN Women, UNHRC, UNCTAD). So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
Statement 1 is wrong: the NDB is headquartered in Shanghai. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So B (2 and 3 only) is right; A and D include statement 1; C omits statement 2.

Egypt joined the NDB (set up by the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration, HQ Shanghai) in 2023. Uzbekistan later became the 10th member and first from Central Asia. Argentina and Indonesia are BRICS-expansion names, not NDB entrants.
The World Bank financed these road-safety highways ($358 mn, June 2023), a question asked before. ADB, NDB and AIIB are other multilateral lenders not linked to this project.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Gulf/West Asia energy and diaspora links are the focus of Link West, not Neighbourhood First. Hence 1 and 2 only; options containing 3 are wrong, and 1 only misses statement 2.
B is correct. A has the wrong venue and the wrong anniversary (75, not 50). C describes the India-Australia 3rd Annual Summit in Melbourne. D describes the EU, India's 22nd FTA partner.

Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 36 IAF Rafales came under the 2016 deal, not 2019. So 1, 3 and 4 only; options with 2 are wrong, and '1 and 3 only' misses the 114-jet AoN.
Nipun (DSRV mother ship) was built by Hindustan Shipyard Ltd, Visakhapatnam, an AP angle. The other shipyards are not linked to Nipun.

OSIRIS-APEX is heading for asteroid Apophis. Bennu is the asteroid from which OSIRIS-REx returned samples in 2023. 2024 YR4 is a separate asteroid in the news. Didymos is not the target of this mission.
INS Mahendragiri is a Project 17A Nilgiri-class stealth frigate associated with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited. It is also placed with the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Agni-4 is a nuclear-capable MRBM (about 4,000 km), not an ICBM. So 1 and 2 only.

Semicon 2.0 / ISM 2.0 has an outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore, with up to 40% capex support for CMOS fabs. Rs 6,003.65 crore is the National Quantum Mission outlay and about Rs 10,372 crore is the IndiaAI Mission outlay. Rs 76,000 crore is not the Semicon 2.0 outlay.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the plan is to grow to 1 lakh genomes, not 10 lakh. So 1 and 2 only.

A is correct: two cubes were gifted to Sri Lanka (2026) and two were sent to Venezuela after its earthquake (Jul 2026). B swaps the countries; C names countries that did not receive them; D gives the wrong reason for the Venezuela dispatch.
HLL Lifecare Limited is the nodal agency for sourcing under Project BHISHM (asked 2024). DRDO, ICMR and HAL are not the sourcing agency.
The 2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025 was held at AIIMS Jhajjar, the National Cancer Institute (asked 2024). The other AIIMS campuses were not the venue.

A is correct: the Guchimi Kumki camp in Parvathipuram-Manyam opened in July 2026. B is wrong because Chittoor has the Musallamadugu camp (Palamaner), not Guchimi. D is wrong because the four female tigers are to come from Maharashtra (Chandrapur) and Madhya Pradesh. No figures are recorded for NSTR anti-poaching camps, so C is not supported.

The Gaja Mitra scheme for human-elephant conflict was approved by the Karnataka Cabinet (asked 2025). Jharkhand hosts India's first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre at Palamu TR; Kerala and Odisha are not linked to Gaja Mitra.

Trinidad and Tobago declared a national emergency over an offshore oil spill in 2024 (PYQ). Iran's Qeshm Island oil spill was in Aug 2026, threatening the Hara mangroves; Sri Lanka is linked to Cyclone Ditwah. Mauritius is not linked to this event.

The HDI was conceived by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq, working with Amartya Sen; UNDP has published the HDR since 1990. Sen contributed but was not the sole originator. Stiglitz and Bhagwati are not linked to the HDI.

India ranked 38th of 139 in LPI 2023, up from 44th in 2018 (PYQ). 44th was the 2018 position; 54th and 22nd are not India's LPI ranks. Note that India's GII 2025 rank is also 38/139, but that index is by WIPO, not the World Bank.

A is the wrong pair: SIPRI ranks India as the 2nd-largest arms importer, with Ukraine 1st, so India is not the largest. B correctly gives India 2nd, and India is 6th in IP/patent filings (WIPO Report 2023) and 3rd in research publications.

Pakistan was the most polluted country (about 13 times the WHO limit) in the World Air Quality Report 2025; Loni (UP) was the most polluted city and India was 6th. India and Bangladesh were not first, and Chad was not first in this edition.
The India Skills Report 2024 named Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala as the top talent States (asked in the exam). The other combinations are incorrect.
Kirsty Coventry (Zimbabwe) is the first woman and the first African to be IOC President (a PYQ fact). She is not Asian or European, and she was not elected unopposed.

The current-relevance angles are the UN Secretary-General race with the first UNSC straw poll (Aug 2026), the Gukesh-Sindarov title match, and IB chief Mahesh Dixit from the AP cadre, so statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 (Justice Lisa Gill as the first woman Chief Justice of the AP High Court) is treated as correct by the key, giving 1, 2, 3 and 4.
